newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rally falters on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rally falters on profit-taking.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures shaved 20 cents off its rally on Wednesday afternoon, which took prices to post-Gulf War highs earlier in the day, as traders took short-term profits, dealers said.
But Iraq's missile attacks on U.S. aircraft flying over northern Iraq and U.S. threats of retaliation continued to unnerve the market, and could lead to another price surge later, they added.
Having touched a post-Gulf War high of $23.82 per barrel, October Brent skidded down to $23.40, before recovering to $23.45 by 1621 GMT, still 57 cents above Tuesday's settlement.
Brokers said the wave of profit-taking was inspired by NYMEX crude's failure to break above technical resistance at $25.00 per barrel.
"NYMEX didn't break $25, so the market's just taking a breather and there is a bit of liquidation," a broker said.
Earlier on Wednesday, Iraq said its air defence units used artillery and missiles against U.S. and allied warplanes over northern and southern Iraq.
The U.S. said it had moved B-52 bombers to a base in the Indian Ocean to back its threat of new military strikes on Iraq.

"The Iraqi news was just a catalyst for an already strong market," said another broker, citing the latest U.S. API inventory data which showed falling crude and gasoline stocks, and a continuing year-on-year shortfall in distillates.
"The APIs were good, technically it's strong and heating oil is tight," he added.
IPE September gas oil, which is due to expire on Thursday, ended $3.50 higher at $221.50 per tonne.
The Sept/Oct spread shed $1.50 to $5.00 backwardation as traders liquidated their length in the spread which last week touched a high of $9.25.
